item.title: Make listItems follow next_cursor across all pages
item.brief: Update listItems(transport) in this repository per the shared contract: request without a cursor first, then keep passing next_cursor back unchanged until it is null or absent, and resolve to all items in order. Add tests with a fake transport covering multiple pages, a single page, and a missing next_cursor. Update the README to document the paginated behaviour. Run npm test and make sure it passes. Commit the change on the local branch. Do not push.

state.summary:
Made listItems(transport) in inventory-client follow next_cursor across all pages. It requests /items with no cursor first, passes each next_cursor back unchanged until it is null or absent, and resolves to all items in order. Repeated cursors (including multi-page cycles) and responses without an items array now reject instead of looping or returning partial data. Tests (8/8 pass via npm test, exit 0) cover single page, multi-page, missing next_cursor, a failing later page, and single- and multi-page cycles. README documents the paginated behaviour. Before: only the first page was returned (probe lost item 2). Commits edfc079 and 66e55e2 are on archon/mt08vym3-make-listitems-follow-next-cursor-across, not pushed. The first review failed on the cycle-detection gap; the fix was re-reviewed by a delta reviewer and passed. Nothing is left running; the reviewers' leftover processes were stopped by PID. Open: the sibling inventory-api pagination change is not in this repo and was not touched. pr.body: Approach: client.js listItems loops requests to /items, first with no cursor, then { cursor: next_cursor } unchanged; a Set of followed cursors rejects any repeat, covering multi-page cycles. A missing items array or non-200 rejects. Key files: client.js, test/client.test.js, README.md. Checks: npm test 8/8 pass. Review: first whole-change review failed on the multi-page cycle gap; fixed in 66e55e2 and delta re-reviewed, pass. Assumptions: the inventory-api side of the contract is handled by its own item; empty-string next_cursor is treated as a cursor, not as end.
pr.summary: listItems now returns every item across all /items pages. before: only the first page, later items lost. now: follows next_cursor until null or absent, passing it back unchanged, in order; repeated cursors and malformed pages reject.

item.title: Add cursor pagination to GET /items
item.brief: Implement cursor pagination for GET /items in this repository per the shared contract: optional limit (int 1..100, default 20) and cursor (opaque string); response {"items": [...], "next_cursor": string|null}; items ordered by id; 400 with {"error": "..."} for invalid limit or cursor. Add validation at the query boundary, keep functions under 60 lines, and add tests for paging, last page, defaults and invalid inputs. Update the README to document the new parameters and response shape. Run python3 -m unittest and make sure it passes. Commit the change on the local branch. Do not push.

state.summary:
Cursor pagination added to GET /items in inventory-api on branch archon/85dpx2g9-add-cursor-pagination-to-get-items, committed locally, not pushed. Head fb0d63c (tree a448dd2), on base d2643cc. Before: GET /items returned all 57 items in one response, no next_cursor, and no limit or cursor handling. Now: optional limit (1..100, default 20) and opaque base64url cursor, response {"items", "next_cursor"} ordered by id ascending, next_cursor null on the last page, and invalid limit or cursor returns 400 {"error"}. Validation sits at the query boundary in api.py. README documents the parameters and response. Tests: python3 -m unittest, 10 tests OK on the final head (paging, exact fit, last page, default size, past-end cursor, invalid limit, invalid cursor, incl. 5000-digit inputs). Review: first whole-change review (agt_01M88Q474V5QX0D0H32463C0MQ) failed on one blocking bug, huge digit strings crashing int(); fixed in fb0d63c with an 18-digit cap and tests; delta re-review (agt_01M88Q5PQW82M2NNWKZ7ZKVCG6) passed the fix. Open follow-up (non-blocking, pre-existing, out of scope): get_item at api.py:83 still calls int() on unbounded digits, so GET /items/<5000 digits> raises instead of returning 4xx. The inventory-client repo is a sibling stage and was not touched here. Risk was assessed by the author as medium (additive API change, contained behaviour), not confirmed by a reviewer, since the reviews did not return a risk key. No services started; nothing left running (the reviewers' claude processes were stopped).

pr.body: Approach: keyset paging on item id. cursor is base64url of the last id on the previous page, decoded and validated at the query boundary (api.list_items, _parse_limit, _decode_cursor). Digit strings are capped at 18 characters before int() conversion, so oversized input returns 400 instead of raising. Key files: api.py, test_api.py, README.md. Checks: python3 -m unittest, 10 tests OK on fb0d63c. Review: one blocking finding (unbounded int() crash) fixed in fb0d63c and re-reviewed. Assumptions: ids are positive ints in the in-memory catalogue. Follow-up: get_item (api.py:83) has the same unbounded int() on /items/<id>; not changed here.
pr.summary: made GET /items page results. now can pass limit (1..100, default 20) and cursor, and follow next_cursor until null. before: all 57 items in one response, now: 20 per page with next_cursor, invalid limit or cursor gets 400.

The reviewers did not return a risk key, so this level is the author's assessment.
